seats.name: builder-2
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named answer.txt in your current working directory.

A reviewer looked at your previous submission (still in this directory) and said:
"""
`PRINT CALL outer 1` should print 100, not 101, because `inner` runs in its own call and can't see `outer`'s local `a`. It reads the global `a`, which is 0, so `+ a b` gives 0 + 100.
"""
Make only the necessary changes to address the reviewer's feedback. This is your final revision; there is no further review round.
seats.text:
I changed `answer.txt` so the second-to-last value is 100 instead of 101. The reviewer is right. `inner` runs in its own call, so it can't see `outer`'s local `a`. It reads the global `a`, which is 0, so `PRINT CALL outer 1` gives 0 + 100. I changed nothing else, and I didn't re-run the rest of the program.

The file now reads:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`
